title: <name> and the Great Holi Color Storm

pages.text: <name> loved Holi, but this year he decided to be extra careful. 'I’ll throw colors gently, no mess, no chaos,' he promised himself. He wore an old t-shirt, kept a small water balloon ready, and even marked a 'safe zone' in the garden.

But as soon as his friends arrived, all that careful planning went out the window. Riya sneaked up with a handful of pink powder, and before <name> could react, pow! Pink dust puffed into his hair and shirt. 'Hey!' he squeaked, trying to dodge.

The color battle escalated quickly. Arjun grabbed a water balloon filled with green color and splashed it right on <name>’s back. Laughing, <name> retaliated with blue powder, sending a cloud floating over the garden fence.
The neighbors peeked, eyes wide, as a rainbow storm swirled around the yard. Then, the mischievous neighborhood cat and dog joined in. The cat pounced on a stray balloon, sending yellow water flying.

The dog rolled through a puddle of colors, chasing the cat, and both dashed around leaving streaks of red, green, and purple everywhere. <name> tried to catch the cat, slipped on wet color, and somersaulted into a pile of pink powder, emerging like a cotton candy sculpture.

The friends started a chaotic chase, running through puddles, slipping on powder, and shrieking with laughter. Colors splashed the walls, the plants, and even the old bicycle in the corner. By now, the entire street looked like a festival of rainbow chaos.

Finally, exhausted but laughing, everyone collapsed on the grass, covered head to toe in every color imaginable. Pink, green, blue, yellow — they looked like walking rainbows. Even the cat and dog were streaked in bright hues.

Mom appeared with a tray of snacks — juicy mango slices, sweet gujiyas, and lemonade. Between bites, <name> wiped powder from his eyes and giggled. 'Well… I guess being careful is boring anyway!' he said.
The friends nodded in agreement. They munched, laughed, and shared stories of who got the most colorful splash, while the sun set over a garden painted in Holi colors.

<name> realized that sometimes the best memories come from the messiest adventures. That day, everyone returned home covered in colors, sticky hands, and huge smiles, already planning the next year’s Holi storm.
